r0.why: Ring-shaped coral rim and lagoon [1], cays on rim [2], small land area [36], under 5 m elevation [37].

r1.why: Corals only in warm (sub)tropics so atolls only there [27,3]; ~440 atolls mostly Pacific/Indian with named groups [4,23,24]; eight Caribbean atolls east of Nicaragua [26].

r2.why: 1842 Beagle explanation [44]; fringing reef, extinct eroded sinking volcano, barrier reef, islets and lagoon not crater [6-10]; growth must match sea level [11].

r3.why: Antecedent karst steps: flat mound during subsidence, exposure and rain dissolution, rim slowest centre fastest, saucer, resubmergence [12-17].

r4.why: Dhivehi atholhu [18], Indo-Aryan language of the Maldives [19], French atollon 1625 and Darwin's 'circular group of coral islets' [20].

r5.why: Kure 28°25'N with NW Hawaiian atolls [28], Elizabeth and Middleton Reefs Tasman Sea [29], Aranuka 13 km from Equator [31,32], Huvadhu 255 islands [43].
